NONE: › a small bus that follows a regular route
（按固定路線行駛的）小公共汽車
› slight uncontrolled movement or shaking, for example in electronic equipment
› to move or shake slightly in an uncontrolled way

example: You may notice jitter on the screen.
你也許注意到了螢幕上的抖動。
This caused the film to jitter.

NONE: › a feeling of nervousness that you experience before something important happens

example: I always get the jitters the morning before an exam.
考試當天早上我總是很緊張。
figurative The collapse of the company has caused jitters in the financial markets.
這家公司的倒閉導致金融市場出現恐慌。

NONE: 緊張不安的；心煩意亂的

example: He felt all jittery before the interview.
面試前他感到非常緊張。
I get really jittery if I drink too much coffee.
我咖啡喝得太多就會發抖。
